reasons: Only 3 of the 8 sections were available, so saving and layout are not checked.
AI errors are only written to the console, with no message for the user.
Starting values do not refresh if a different task is passed in while the modal stays open.

terms.meaning: typing a sentence and letting an AI fill in the form fields
a helper that talks to an outside AI service on the app's behalf
the developer log in the browser where error messages are written

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in React, icons, task types, the store, form components, the AI provider and the voice button. This section only sets up the file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond normal file setup.
sections.watch_out: The AI provider import means text typed for quick-add is sent to an outside AI service.

sections.name: TaskCreateModalProps
sections.title: Props: open flag, close action, existing task
sections.what: Defines the modal's inputs: whether it is open, a function to close it, and an optional existing task used to pre-fill the form.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same form creates new tasks and edits existing ones.
sections.watch_out: Starting values are read only once, when the modal first appears, so passing a different task later can leave the old values on screen.

sections.name: TaskCreateModal (part 1)
sections.title: Form state and AI quick-add
sections.what: Creates one piece of remembered state per field, starting from the existing task or from defaults such as high priority and a 45-minute estimate. The AI step copies the parsed fields into the form and shows a success note. When closed, the modal draws nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each field's value separate, so the user can edit any one of them before saving.
sections.watch_out: If the AI request fails, the only sign is a console message, so the user is not told why the fields did not fill.

sections.name: TaskCreateModal (part 2)
sections.title: Saving the form
sections.what: Runs when the form is submitted. It checks that a title exists, turns the comma-separated tags into a clean list, then either updates the existing task or adds a new one, and closes the window.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same form serves both creating and editing, so one save handler chooses the action based on whether an existing task was passed in.
sections.watch_out: A blank or zero time estimate is silently saved as 30 minutes, and a newly added task always starts with zero minutes spent and no dependencies.

sections.name: TaskCreateModal (part 3)
sections.title: Header and AI quick-fill box
sections.what: Draws the window heading, which reads Edit Task or Create New Task, and the highlighted box at the top where a user types a sentence and presses Enter or the Auto-Fill button. A microphone button can add spoken words to the same box.
sections.why: Likely reason: the AI box comes first so a user can describe a task in plain words instead of filling every field by hand.
sections.watch_out: The parsing function behind Auto-Fill is defined outside the shown lines, so its success and failure paths cannot be checked here.

sections.name: TaskCreateModal (part 4)
sections.title: Title, description, status and priority fields
sections.what: Shows the required title box, the description box, and two dropdowns: status (todo, doing, blocked, waiting, completed, cancelled) and priority (P1 Urgent to P4 Low). Each field stays in sync with the form values.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the exact list, though the same six statuses appear on the other task screens.
sections.watch_out: The status and priority values are type casts, so a value outside the expected list would be saved without any check.

sections.name: TaskCreateModal (part 5)
sections.title: Energy, dates, estimate, project and category fields
sections.what: Shows dropdowns for energy level and linked project, plus boxes for due date, due time, estimated minutes and category. The project choices come from the saved project list.
sections.why: Likely reason: these fields let the user plan when a task is due, how long it takes, how much energy it needs and which project it belongs to.
sections.watch_out: Clearing the minutes box stores zero while typing, and the save step then turns that into 30, so the user may not see what will be saved.

sections.name: TaskCreateModal (part 6)
sections.title: Tags, subtasks, notes and buttons
sections.what: Shows the tags box, the subtask builder where steps are added and removed, the notes box, and the Cancel and Create or Update buttons. The submit button label changes when editing an existing task.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for this order; tags are typed as comma-separated text and converted when saved.
sections.watch_out: The functions that add subtasks are defined outside the shown lines, so how new subtask ids are created cannot be verified here.

summary: A pop-up form for creating or editing a task, with an AI quick-add that fills the fields from a sentence.
purpose: Lets the user enter full task details, or describe a task in plain words and let the AI fill in the fields.
why: Likely reason: one form serves both new tasks and edits, starting from an existing task when one is given.
how: Holds each field's value in its own state, starting from the existing task or from defaults. The AI step sends the typed sentence to a provider and copies the reply into the fields. The rest of the form, including saving, subtasks and layout, is in sections not included in this packet.
inputs: The open flag, a close function, an optional existing task, typed field values, and the sentence for the AI step.
outputs: Form values on screen, and AI-filled fields. Saving is not visible in the sections provided.
risks: Saving and most of the form are not visible here, so save behaviour cannot be checked. AI failures show nothing to the user beyond a console message. Starting values are read only once when the modal first opens.
debug: If fields do not update for a new task, check how the modal is opened and whether it stays mounted. If the AI does nothing, check the browser console for the parse error and the provider setup. If saved data is wrong, check the sections not included here.
